threads_text: Hackers posted fake desktop apps called GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus on GitHub, and they still ranked near the top of Google. The installer inside is a real signed OpenAI or Anthropic file that quietly loads malware and turns your PC into a crypto miner. Where do you download your AI apps from?
caption:
Check Point Research found fake GitHub projects posing as AI desktop apps called GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus.
Each download hides a malicious file next to a real, signed OpenAI or Anthropic installer, and the final payload in this campaign was a crypto miner.
The fake pages still ranked near the top of Google results.

Have you ever downloaded an AI app from somewhere other than the official site?

paragraphs.text: Check Point Research published a report on October 27, 2026, describing a malware campaign that used fake GitHub projects dressed up as AI desktop apps. The fake apps carried the names GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus, and the researchers say they tracked the operation, which they call Yoba, for about two months.

The projects relied on ordinary GitHub features. Landing pages hosted on GitHub Pages offered download buttons that pointed to ZIP files stored in the projects' releases. Check Point said the repositories showed no fake stars or forks, yet they still appeared among the top results on Google, which the researchers attribute most likely to search engine poisoning.
How the trusted installer was abused

Each ZIP file contained a legitimate signed program named Setup.exe from OpenAI or, in the Claude package, from Anthropic. Beside it sat a malicious file named winmm.dll, which imitates a standard Windows library. When the signed program starts, it loads that file, a technique known as DLL sideloading that lets malicious code run under a trusted name. Check Point noted that the archives were not password protected and still had very low detection rates.

The first stage, which Check Point calls YobaDropper, runs only when its host is named Setup.exe, requires administrator rights and skips computers set to Russian and several other languages of former Soviet countries. It copies its files into a folder under ProgramData and creates a scheduled task, labeled as a Microsoft component, that starts three minutes after each boot.

The second stage, YobaLoader, reads the profile picture of a Telegram channel and uses its last 50 bytes to generate a domain name. It then asks Google's DNS over HTTPS service for a text record holding an encrypted command, checks the command's signature and downloads the next file from the Catbox file host. In this campaign, the final payload was the XMRig 6.26.0 cryptominer, which connected through Tor. The researchers warned that the loader could deliver other payloads in later waves.

The first repository was created on July 16, 2026, and the fake GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus and GPT-6 Astra archives were uploaded between August 30 and September 4, according to Check Point. An earlier version of the dropper seen in early June 2026 was loaded by a program named Cursor.exe. The researchers said the operator shows indicators of Russian origin, while Cyber Security News noted that these clues do not prove who is responsible. Check Point did not publish any victim count.

Check Point advised caution with AI helper tools downloaded from unverified repositories and recommended policies that restrict software from unknown sources. Cyber Security News added that users should check a repository's owner, account age and commit history before running anything, and that defenders should watch for signed programs loading DLL files from user folders.

The campaign shows how attackers follow attention. Names of popular or rumored AI models draw searches, and a signed file from a well known AI company lends the download credibility it has not earned. The signature on Setup.exe was real; the problem was the file placed next to it.
Watch whether GitHub removes the remaining repositories and whether new fake AI app names appear in search results, since Check Point says the same loader can carry a different payload next time.
